text: What if we're the last generation of humans who actually have to think?
For thousands of years, intelligence was our greatest survival tool.
we learn to build fires, create civilizations, and eventually invent machines that could do our physical labor.
But now, we're building machines that can do our thinking.
Machines that can write, create, reason, and maybe one day understand the universe better than we ever could.
and here's the part nobody really talks about.
What happens when intelligence is no longer what makes humanity special?
Maybe the question isn't whether artificial intelligence will become more human.
Maybe it's whether humans will remember what it means to be human.
